chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ وَجَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ، عَن أَبَانَ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: From Ibn Masud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abi Basir who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قِيلَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ – وَأَنَا عِنْدَهُ -: إِنَّ سَالِمَ بْنَ أَبِي حَفْصَةَ يَرْوِي عَنْكَ أَنَّكَ تَتَكَلَّمُ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ وَجْهًا لَكَ مِنْ كُلِّهَا الْمَخْرَجُ

translations.en: It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him: "Salim ibn Abi Hafsa narrates from you that you speak with seventy facets, for each facet you have a way out."

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ: مَا يُرِيدُ سَالِمُ مِنِّي؟ أَيُرِيدُ أَنْ أَجِيءَ بِالْمَلَائِكَةِ؟ فَوَاللَّهَ مَا جَاءَتْ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ

translations.en: So he said: "What does Salim want from me? Does he want me to come with the angels?! For by Allah, not even the prophets came with them."

chunks.arabic_text: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ وَاللَّهَ مَا كَانَ سَقِيمًا وَمَا كَذَبَ

translations.en: And Ibrahim had said, 'I am sick,' and by Allah he was not sick, nor did he lie.

chunks.arabic_text: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا وَمَا فَعَلَهُ وَمَا كَذَبَ

translations.en: And Ibrahim also said: 'Rather, this, the biggest one of them has done it,' while he had not done it, nor did he lie.

chunks.arabic_text: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ: إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ وَاللَّهَ مَا كَانُوا سَارِقِينَ وَمَا كَذَبَ

translations.en: And Yusuf said: 'You are thieves,' and by Allah they were not thieves, nor did he lie.

en.summary: The Imam (AS) addresses the claim that he speaks with 'se seventy facets' (each having a way out to avoid lying) by citing the prophets Ibrahim and Yusuf. He argues that if the prophets spoke in a way that was technically true but not literally what was meant (e.g., Ibrahim saying 'I am sick' when he was healthy, or Yusuf saying 'You are thieves' when they were innocent), they did not lie. Thus, speaking with multiple facets is a valid form of truthfulness, not deception.
en.seo_question: How do Shia scholars explain the concept of 'seventy facets' in hadith without implying the Imam lied?
